title: API: MemoryBackend struct missing #[non_exhaustive]
description:
memory.rs:229:
    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
    pub struct MemoryBackend { inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner>> }

Has no #[non_exhaustive].

What callers cannot depend on / what locks the maintainer:
- Adding a public field is a breaking change. Even with the only existing field 'inner' being private, the lack of #[non_exhaustive] means the maintainer cannot add a new pub field later (e.g. a config Arc, a metrics counter, a tracing span name) without a major version bump.
- More subtly: callers cannot pattern-match an empty struct (there is nothing to match), but they CAN construct via MemoryBackend::default() / new() / new_with_accounts(...). #[non_exhaustive] would not break that. Adding the attribute now is risk-free and reserves the design space.

Recommendation:
- Add #[non_exhaustive] to MemoryBackend.
- The canonical sibling (jmap-mail-server::memory::MemoryBackend at memory.rs:251) is similarly missing #[non_exhaustive]. Per workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template rule, change the canonical first, then propagate.

What goes wrong if this stays:
- Forces a major-version cycle for what would otherwise be a non-breaking field addition. The 'memory' feature mitigation (lib.rs:28 declares API stability is opt-in via feature) covers this for now, but the same applies to MemoryError — the discipline costs nothing pre-1.0.
close_reason: Triage 2026-10-31 at c07d5206: fixed: MemoryBackend is #[non_exhaustive] in every extension-server, e.g. crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/mod.rs:406; metadata MemoryBackend deleted in b34a07bf
